paragraphs.source_en: Whether the prospect picks up the telephone or answers the door, it’s time to execute, and it’s do or die. The lukewarm sales call begins with the Introduction stage. Although the Introduction is the shortest of the four stages, generally lasting only fifteen to forty-five seconds, it’s a mistake to discount the significance of an effective opening. Our objective in the Introduction stage is very straightforward. We are simply trying to get one foot in the door in order to secure a few minutes of the prospect’s time and attention. While this may sound easy, experienced salespeople are keenly aware that the beginning of the initial sales call is one of the highest hurdles in the sales process.

paragraphs.source_en: In reality, salespeople know that it can take thirty, forty-five, or even sixty minutes to uncover needs and communicate value, but once the prospect realizes you are a salesperson, it’s more likely you only have thirty, forty-five, or sixty seconds. Cautious prospects form their impressions very quickly, and as a salesperson, you aren’t likely to get a second chance. Therefore, how you choose to manage this window of opportunity will likely determine whether your call ends abruptly or you succeed in getting that foot in the door.
